content: Quest Academy is a small, independent educational institution specifically designed for gifted and talented children. It is located in Palatine, Illinois. The school holds accreditation from the Independent Schools Association of the Central States (ISACS) and is a member of both the National Association of Independent Schools (NAIS) and the National Association for Gifted Children (NAGC). The annual tuition for one child is $16,000 USD. Financial aid is available and is awarded based on demonstrated need. Each grade level has two classes, except for preschool, which has only two classes in total. The school building has two stories, with grades 3 through 8 located on the second floor. Band sessions are conducted in a separate building that was previously part of a plaza. Preschool classes are also held in a separate building. Additionally, there is a store on campus where Quest-branded apparel and other items can be purchased. The school was originally established in 1982 under the name Creative Children's Academy. It was founded by parents seeking an alternative educational environment for gifted children who were struggling in public schools. In 1988, the school achieved full accreditation from ISACS. In 1993, the local park district, which owned the school’s facility at the time, announced plans to demolish the building. In response, two school administrators collaborated with the school board to purchase the former Palatine Public Library, which was then remodeled into a school facility. The school was renamed Quest Academy in 1999, and a capital campaign funded the addition of a gymnasium and a performing arts wing. Quest Academy has a no-cut sports policy, ensuring that all students can participate in athletic activities. The middle school athletic teams include boys' and girls' cross country, basketball, soccer, volleyball, and track. These teams compete against other small, independent schools with similar educational philosophies. The school offers a variety of extracurricular activities, including a journalism club, the Knight Program, buddy groups, and the Birthday Bomb Club. The journalism club produces a student newspaper and an annual publication called Myriastella, which features student writings and poems. The student council operates under the Knight Program, which requires students to complete a community service project to earn the title of knight. Monthly assemblies, referred to as pageants, are held on the first Monday of each month to recognize new knights and commend squires for demonstrating good character. Other extracurricular opportunities include an extensive community service program and an after-school activity focused on stock market education. Quest Academy also participates in several math competitions, including events at The Latin School of Chicago and Mathcounts. Two individuals from the school have won notable prizes in these competitions. The curriculum at Quest Academy is designed to provide gifted students with an environment where they can excel at their own pace across various subjects. The academic program includes mathematics, language arts, social studies, art, drama, science, music, French, technology, and library studies. Additionally, trimester-long elective classes are offered several days a week, allowing students to explore specialized interests.
